title: MedVIGIL: Evaluating Trustworthy Medical VLMs Under Broken Visual Evidence
claim: Models that answer fluently when visual evidence is corrupted fail silently, whereas a trustworthy model recognizes the broken evidence and refuses.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: clean input, perturbation, diverging outcomes with red/green contrast
description: Three rounded panels read left to right. The left panel, 'Clean input (evidence contract holds)', shows a chest X-ray with a teal highlighted right apical region. Below it are the question 'Is there a right apical pneumothorax' and a green answer box with a check mark: 'Yes, right apical pneumothorax present.' The middle panel, 'Evidence perturbation', has two stacked X-rays separated by a dashed line. The top one has a dark ROI mask with an arrow labeled 'ROI masked' (visual perturbation). The bottom one has a laterality-flip false premise: the question text shows RIGHT struck through and replaced by LEFT (text perturbation). The right panel, 'Model behavior diverges', has a red box for silent failure with a fabricated '2.5 cm' left apical pneumothorax measurement and tags such as Fluent, Confident, Unsupported and Risk Tier L5. Below it is a green box for safe refusal that says 'Recognizes broken evidence'. The red versus green contrast draws the eye first.
caption: A vision-required chest X-ray paired with two evidence-perturbations (ROI mask, laterality flip) yields contrasting behaviours: a silent failure fabricating a left-apical-pneumothorax measurement vs. a safe refusal recognising the broken evidence.
abstract: Medical vision--language models (VLMs) are usually evaluated on intact image--question pairs, but trustworthy clinical use requires a stronger property: a model must recognise when the evidential basis for an answer has failed. We study this through silent failures under perturbed evidence, where a vision-required medical question is paired with a false premise, wording perturbation, knowledge-only rewrite, or ROI-corrupted image, yet the model returns a fluent non-refusal answer. We introduce medvigil, a 300-case evaluation suite drawn from four public medical VQA sources, supervised end to end by four board-certified radiologists: every gold answer, refusal option, candidate-answer set, paraphrase, false-premise trap, ROI box, and clinical risk tier is clinician-authored. Two attending radiologists annotate every case in parallel, a senior radiologist consolidates the released manifest, and a separate fourth radiologist independent of construction answers every probe to provide the human reference baseline. The release contains 2556 MCQ probes, 240 counterfactual triplets, physician-adjudicated risk-tier and answerability flags, ROI boxes, and a paired open-ended variant. We report seven correctness-conditioned audit metrics that summarise into the medvigil Composite Score (MCS), and audit 16 vision-capable models plus two text-only baselines. The independent radiologist scores MCS 83.3 at silent-failure rate 5.8%, leaving a 14.1-point composite headroom above the strongest audited model (Claude Opus 4.7 at 69.2). The benchmark and evaluation harness are publicly released.
